messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: Error reading genalex file
parts:
Hello Jennifer,

Thank you for giving a detailed description of your error and examples of data to produce the error.

I believe this is an error that originated in the "adegenet" package, specifically with the function "df2genind". Basically, your sample names were being interpreted as numbers instead of names.This issue was fixed some time ago on the development version of adegenet. 

Both adegenet and poppr are actually set to have new versions released soon. You can see what's modified in poppr here and see what's modified in adegenet here. 

You can install the development versions of adegenet and poppr using the package "devtools". Since you're on a Windows system, be sure to install Rtools first.

devtools::install_github(c("thibautjombart/adegenet", "grunwaldlab/poppr"))


Best,
Zhian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: Error reading genalex file
parts:
Hi Jessica,

You threw a real curveball on that one. The problem here lies in some of the allele calls for your Rosie1 locus. You have some alleles denoted as "18.5".

The reason why this doesn't work is because adegenet is not expecting alleles to be fractional. The genind object is constructed such that each column represents an allele and is denoted as [Locus].[Allele]. This convention is used so the program can easily work with alleles and loci in a predictable fashion. When you have a column called "Rosie1.18.5", it becomes unclear whether the locus is called "Rosie1.18" or if the allele is "18.5". 

My suggested solution: Multiply all of those values by 2 before they come into R, so you will get integers. 

If you wanted to use these values for Bruvo's distance: 

1. Half-steps violate the assumptions of the model for stepwise mutation. 
2. All values are rounded to integers before calculation, thus the value of 18.5 will become 18 (R rounds using the IEC 60559 standard, which is "go to the even digit"). 

Hope that helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.

Zhian

On Monday, November 23, 2015 at 11:29:33 AM UTC-6, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hi Jessica,

You threw a real curveball on that one. The problem here lies in some of the allele calls for your Rosie1 locus. You have some alleles denoted as "18.5".

The reason why this doesn't work is because adegenet is not expecting alleles to be fractional. The genind object is constructed such that each column represents an allele and is denoted as [Locus].[Allele]. This convention is used so the program can easily work with alleles and loci in a predictable fashion. When you have a column called "Rosie1.18.5", it becomes unclear whether the locus is called "Rosie1.18" or if the allele is "18.5". 

My suggested solution: Multiply all of those values by 2 before they come into R, so you will get integers. 

If you wanted to use these values for Bruvo's distance: 

1. Half-steps violate the assumptions of the model for stepwise mutation. 
2. All values are rounded to integers before calculation, thus the value of 18.5 will become 18 (R rounds using the IEC 60559 standard, which is "go to the even digit"). 

Hope that helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.

Zhian

On Sunday, November 22, 2015 at 12:58:30 PM UTC-6, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hello Jennifer,

Thank you for giving a detailed description of your error and examples of data to produce the error.

I believe this is an error that originated in the "adegenet" package, specifically with the function "df2genind". Basically, your sample names were being interpreted as numbers instead of names.This issue was fixed some time ago on the development version of adegenet. 

Both adegenet and poppr are actually set to have new versions released soon. You can see what's modified in poppr here and see what's modified in adegenet here. 

You can install the development versions of adegenet and poppr using the package "devtools". Since you're on a Windows system, be sure to install Rtools first.

devtools::install_github(c("thibautjombart/adegenet", "grunwaldlab/poppr"))


Best,
Zhian
